rationale: Close the remaining boundaries of the Node-wrapper question with source reasoning: the closed proposal channel exists only for the removal case (the local node's Progress entry disappears while it was present), a demotion keeps that entry and therefore leaves the channel open, and an addition never re-opens a closed channel - so the state persists until the leadership changes with a leader known, and Node.Propose can report it only through the caller's context or the node's done channel, with no distinct error. The measured account and its receipt are unchanged; the discriminator keeps only the group-size variant as an unmeasured item.

knowledge.statement: The Node wrapper closes its proposal channel only when an applied configuration change makes the local node's Progress entry disappear (the guard requires the node to have been in Progress before, to be absent after, and to appear in neither Voters nor VotersOutgoing); a demotion to learner keeps the Progress entry and therefore does not close the channel, and applying a change that adds the node back takes the okBefore=false path, so an addition never re-opens a channel that a removal closed. The only site that re-opens it is the branch that reacts to a change of r.lead while a leader is known.
knowledge.conditions: Node wrapper driven through ApplyConfChange; Config.StepDownOnRemoval false so the node can keep leading or following without its Progress entry being removed.

knowledge.statement: Node.Propose cannot report a closed proposal channel as such: with the channel nil the call waits on a select over that channel, the caller's context and the node's done channel, so it returns only ctx.Err() or ErrStopped, which are the same results an ordinary lost proposal or a stopped node produces.
knowledge.conditions: Node.Propose/stepWait while node.run has set propc to nil.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the same closed state is reached in a group larger than two voters, where a re-added node's Progress entry is recreated by the changer in a different position and the leader may not be the same node that removed it.

interpretations.rationale: The measured account is unchanged: source side, node.run sets its proposal channel to nil when an applied configuration change removes the local node from Progress and the node is in neither voter list (node.go:400-432) and restores it from n.propc only in the branch that reacts to a change of r.lead with a leader known (node.go:343-380), while Node.Propose sends into that channel so a nil channel makes the call wait for the caller's context or the node's done channel (node.go:514-551); receipt c53145c01ad94b449ca1c8b81fe8d7b4 measures the whole arc on a conforming prefix - the controls hold and the leader's log advances before the removal (parsed index 1), the two premises hold on the witness event (index 4: the leader's configuration contains node 2 again and the node still knows leader 1 in the same term), both witness assertions are violated (index 4: Propose returns only when its 300ms deadline fires and the group's log does not change), and the restore comparisons hold once the wrapped node wins a leadership change (index 5: StateLeader at term 2; index 6: no error and the commit index advances 5 to 6). This update adds the boundaries that the source fixes: the closed state requires the removal case, because the guard needs the local node's Progress entry to disappear - a demotion to learner keeps that entry and leaves the channel open - and an addition takes the okBefore=false path, so it never re-opens a channel a removal closed; the only repair site is the leadership-change branch, which is why the measured restore works and why the state persists while the same leader remains. It also records that the wrapper offers no distinct signal for this state: Propose can only return ctx.Err() or ErrStopped, the same results an ordinary lost proposal or a stopped node produces, so a caller that uses a deadline cannot tell the closed channel from a lost proposal except by the node's own status. The remaining unmeasured item is the group-size variant named in the question's discriminator.
counterevidence: The controls hold in the receipt (parsed index 1), so the blocked behaviour is specific to the state after the removal and the re-add rather than a general property of the wrapper.
The restore comparisons hold (parsed indices 5 and 6), so the fault is bounded by the leadership rather than permanent, and the source's repair mechanism is confirmed by measurement.
A demotion to learner does not reach the closed state: the guard requires the local Progress entry to disappear, so the demotion case leaves the proposal channel open.

The Node.Propose documentation warns that proposals can be lost without notice (node.go:138-140), so a caller with a deadline and retries is not blocked; the source shows the wrapper cannot distinguish this state from that warning's case.
limitations: The harness drives a wrapped node against a bare raft instance, so the wrapper's asynchronous ready/advance contract is exercised on one side only, and both nodes run in one process; the leader is installed directly before the removal and the campaign is driven through the wrapper's own Campaign.
The proposed calls use a 300ms deadline: the receipt measures that the call did not complete within it and that the group's log did not change, not the exact duration of the closed channel.

The exercised group has two voters; whether a larger group reaches the same state (where the re-added node's Progress entry is recreated in a different position, and the leader that removed it may not be the leader that re-adds it) is not measured.

Whether an application is expected to keep proposing through a node that has been removed and re-added is itself part of the question; the library's own comment calls the mechanism unsound rather than documenting an intended semantics.

knowledge.assertion: The proposal channel is closed by the removal guard and restored only by a leadership change with a leader known.
With a nil proposal channel Propose blocks until the caller's context or the node's done channel fires.
Only a removal closes the channel; a demotion keeps the Progress entry and an addition never re-opens it.
Propose can only return ctx.Err() or ErrStopped for this state, with no distinct error.
